correctness.rationale: For every finite d>=2 and positive halfwidths, exact integration over all 2d facets gives G(t)=C[phi(t-a)+phi(t+a)+Lambda(Phi(t+a)-Phi(t-a))]. The derivative has the strictly positive prefactor 2C phi(a)exp(-t^2/2)cosh(at) times f(t)=(a-Lambda)tanh(at)-t. For a-Lambda>0, f is strictly concave for t>0, with f(0)=0, f'(0)=a(a-Lambda)-1 and f(t)->-infinity, yielding the precise global sign classification, all maximizers, and the positive-root uniqueness. Direct integration or the derivative Taylor expansion yields quartic critical flatness and the sharp square-root/positive-gain coefficients. Standalone stdlib verification ran successfully (3046 checks), including direct facet Gaussian quadrature in dimensions two and three, random phase tests in dimensions two through nine, and near-critical scaling. Finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Gaussian boundary measure is a central geometric/isoperimetric functional, while fixed-shape translation is a natural optimization orbit because Gaussian density breaks Euclidean translation invariance. The result completely resolves that orbit for every full-dimensional orthotope in all finite dimensions, gives an exact lateral Gaussian facet-to-mass threshold, and demonstrates and classifies a genuine two-maximizer symmetry-breaking phase. Sharp quartic criticality, square-root displacement and quadratic gain provide structural stability, not merely a routine special-case estimate. The transverse geometry enters through a nontrivial sum of hazard-type boundary-to-mass ratios.
